assessment.label: Supported hypothesis (team level): medication cabinet restock. Corroborated by operational records and 4 separate comments.
reasons: Survey: material fall on q07 -0.82, q02 -0.81, q06 -0.33 (team level, n=11 to 13).

brief.obstacle: Medication cabinet restock delayed to 07:00 causing the 06:00 medication pass to run late — supported hypothesis.

evidence_for.claim: Staff report cabinets not filled until 07:00 and passes run late.
Late-dose rate in the 06–07 hour rose from 8.1% to 17.7%, signalling a problem at that hour band.
Per SOP, cabinets should be restocked by 05:00 so stock is available for the 06:00 pass.
Staff report reduced availability of materials, matching a significant drop in the 'materials' survey item.
Team climate worsened on 'my opinions seem to count' and 'someone encourages my development' concurrent with materials decline.

evidence_against.claim: A staffing shortage month (March) could alternatively explain delays on some shifts.
Missed-dose counts show no clear upward trend across the year.

missing: Pharmacy restock timestamps or signed restock reports to confirm actual restock times.
Pharmacy technician staffing levels and overnight workload data.
Unit-level inventory/par-level reports showing which items were below par.
Linkage between individual late doses and cabinet stockouts for 06:00 passes.
brief.owner: Pharmacy Operations Manager, Priya Singh (Medication cabinet restocking schedule)
brief.proposed_test: 30-day test: require pharmacy to restore ADCs by 05:00 daily and record signed restock reports; success = 06:00–07:00 late-dose rate reduced to at or below 8.1%; review on day 30.
brief.limits: Small team survey sample and six wave-2 comments limit generalizability; ops signal is an hourly band observation, not a causal proof (S6, T1, O7).

response.question: Did the Westbrook Telemetry Day team really decline?
response.message: Who responded on Westbrook Telemetry Day: under-one-year employees were 54.5% of respondents in Wave 1 and 0.0% in Wave 2 (respondents 11 and 6). That is a large change in who answered, so part of any movement in the team mean can be a response-mix effect rather than a real change. The team grand mean moved -0.45 (4.26 to 3.81). Holding each tenure band at its company-wide mean, the change in who responded alone would move it -0.20; the remaining -0.25 is within normal variation for 6 respondents. Verdict: mostly a change in who responded, not a real decline. Watch item, not a finding.
